utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning. As you can see, only two judges are present today. Judge Mindua, due to an urgent activity, he can't sit with us today. The Chamber has decided to sit only with two judges pursuant to Rule 15 bis. The witness shall be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to tell you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tolimir, is -- I'm not sure, did you finish yesterday your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I said yesterday that I had a question, I meant the first subject from the first day of Ms. Gallagher's testimony. I would now concentrate on the second area of her testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Gallagher. Peace into this house, I hope that this day of trial will end in keeping with God's will, not mine. In your evidence, you said that you had occasion to view, and that we will also have an opportunity to view in the courtroom, other video footage about people gathering in the town, footage other than what is in the video. Apart from the footage from Susnjari in 1995, is there any other video footage available about how the column, the Muslim column, in Jaglici came to be formed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection is -- is that the -- at least the footage that I have seen is from that particular individual who we saw shot the footage himself, both in Srebrenica and when the column left Srebrenica towards Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you inquire whether anyone else filmed the Muslim column as it was departing towards Susnjari or during the breakout into the territory controlled by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. Not for the purposes of testifying on behalf of this trial video, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 29th of September, on page 53993 [as interpreted], lines 8 through 14, you said, I quote: "In 1999, we have received some video footage. You will see on the video prepared for the trial by Antelope Productions for the movie 'A Cry from the Grave,' broadcast on the BBC, and after that we asked for all the raw footage that was used in making the 'A Cry from the Grave,' they gave us this raw footage." And on page 5995, lines 6 through 9, you said you received a lot of material from Reuters. And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear which network.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: Where do all these BBC, Reuters, and other compilations come from? Where did they get this raw footage? Did you perhaps inquire into that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before the witness will answer your question, I would like to know the correct page number. I think its wrong, what I can read in the transcript. Mr. Gajic, perhaps you can help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone, Mr. President. The references 5993, lines 8 through 14, and 5995, lines 6 through 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, are you able to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The footage that we got from Antelope Productions, they had received from numerous placers, including WTN, Reuters, Poly Archives, BBC, from all different sources. And you'll see -- you've seen much of that footage also from Srpska Radio TV. So in terms of where WTN and Reuters and BBC got their footage, that part we don't know for sure. We see the same footage pretty much everywhere around the world when we've seen the footage of Srebrenica and Potocari and along the road. We know that there were, as we saw in the video, several Srpska Radio TV journalists, and, as well as we know, there were some cameramen attached to the military that were there. My presumption is that the raw footage originally came from them, and it was sold to WTN, Reuters, BBC, all various networks around the world. Antelope Productions got it from them, put together this video, "A Cry from the Grave," and then we received both that documentary that Antelope Productions made as well as all the footage that they had used in putting together their documentary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you had occasion to speak with the cameraman who made the footage that you received from the BBC and other broadcasting companies?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you ask television Sarajevo to provide you with the footage they had of the column and their own films that they made using the footage by (redacted) and other cameramen, films that were later broadcast?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the OTP received footage from Television Sarajevo, from the Sarajevo police, from Srpska Radio TV, directly years prior. So I know we did get footage from all those sources. I personally -- it was before I came to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But later on when you joined the OTP, did you have occasion to check the authenticity of the footage received before you joined the OTP, footage received from other sources such as cameramen and directly, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And first if I can actually just clarify my last response, in terms of requesting footage from TV Sarajevo, Srpska Radio TV, all different sources, it was for all footage regarding anything to do with the Srebrenica operation. It wasn't specifically about the column. So I just wanted to clarify that bit. In terms of checking the authenticity before I joined the OTP, no. I've certainly looked at quite a bit of footage, both from open sources, from what is available, has been available in the ICTY, of anything regarding Srebrenica and Zepa, so I've seen a lot of different footage. You see much of the exact same footage that we've seen in the trial video. It's very repetitive [Realtime transcript read in error "representative"]. It's fairly obvious that it was very limited the sources -- the source material that we, and perhaps the world, received regarding Srebrenica. When we have also requested any existing footage from -- through governmental requests and we have not received anything in recent years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, did you say, it is very representative or it is very repetitive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Repetitive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You were not recorded correctly with this word. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was received prior to me coming to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When he turned over his video, he had made a statement. So there is a witness statement from him to one of our investigators explaining the footage, how he received it, and how it was turned over. And I can give you an ERN number for his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That's not why I'm asking. I think the Defence team has this statement. What I really wanted to know is why filming was interrupted just before arrival to Susnjari; whereas, there is video footage of the moment when the column was arriving at Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember from his statement is that he had run out of -- his battery had died at, I think it was, like, 15-something hundred hours, on the 11th, and so that's where it ended. And as I mentioned before, he was going to even throw away his camera and he met an acquaintance who said he would carry it for him. And then when they both ended up making it to Tuzla, he was able to get his camera and the video back. But for him the filming ended because the battery died.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since these persons documented these activities, (redacted) and this friend of his, do you know if anyone from the OTP spoke to them about the circumstances under which the column moved and broke out from Susnjari to Tuzla, and is there any record of that? Did any of these two men testify about this before a national court or the international tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the statement was only taken of (redacted), and no, I am not aware that he's testified anywhere at all. He was -- the statement was taken in, I think, 2002, and that's it, as far as I am aware, that's the only statement that was taken from him, other than returning the tape to him at another meeting at that time. And, yeah, you see from the statement he mainly is describing what he had videotaped. So it's not a extensive statement about the column and the movements of the column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but if we could, out of an abundance of caution, delete the reference to -- it's page 5, line 24, to the person's name. You know, I now recall that there was a request for confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't recall that. Was it a request from the government or his own? I am not sure about that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It was -- it was from the witness. I -- it's from my recollection, and now I remember the effort we made. If you recall, I think we are talking about the same video where we blocked out family members, including the cameraman. I think that's who we are talking about, so if we could just keep that confidential, I think -- I know that it would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will redact that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise to Mr. McCloskey. I did not know about the understanding between him and the gentleman whose name has to be redacted, but it would have been useful if I had known about the testimony he gave about the column. Could we now move to Exhibit P624, page 5 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You can see on this photograph, this Praga was mentioned many times. You even identified the license number. My question is: Did you investigate this yourself or did you present in your answers, in your evidence, the results of investigations by other people?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I did was verify that the registration number and that it was a Zvornik -- it was registered to the Zvornik Brigade. So I looked at the vehicle logs, looked at the original vehicle logs, just to make sure that this was accurate information. But as I did not make this book, it was not my initial investigation, I just verified that it was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly that you said you checked this only on the basis of papers, not on the spot?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not tracked down the Praga to look at it on the spot. I verified it by the vehicle logs, by the original Zvornik Brigade vehicle logs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see locations and time, and it says 11 July. Why were you not able to determine the exact date when this photograph was made?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we raise this sheet a little, show the top so the witness can understand what I am asking. I thank the electronic courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you now see what I am talking about? Why does it say 10 or 11 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, at the time the book and the video was made, it was not known whether it was the 10th or 11th, and we still don't know if it's the 10th or 11th. There was a lot of movement along the road during that time, and particularly the tanks and the Pragas were moving, as you will see from the vehicle logs, were in movement during those days. We know they were in the general area but haven't been able to determine, you know, that particular footage, if that was on the 10th or 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P624, page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here again we see it's written 10 or 11 July. Were you able in your investigation into Srebrenica to determine the exact date? Below the photograph of Mr. Jolovic, again it says 10 or 11 July. Were you able to find out the exact date in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, obviously, it wasn't known whether it was the 10th or 11th. It was with the testimony of Vinko Pandurevic where he looked at this video while on the stand, and his recollection was he thought it was on the 10th when Legenda is giving orders to his troops, to the Drina Wolves to move, and he believed that it was right after the counter-attack and that they are overlooking Pusmamici [phoen] village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We saw on the video that Mr. Jolovic says, I am on the hard surface or section, and you say it was before the attack. Was it outside the protected area or inside the protected area?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, looking -- I know from looking at the map, it is, I think, roughly about, maybe 5 kilometres from Srebrenica. In terms of his exact location, I'm not a hundred per cent sure. I believe this was, you know, close to the border. I am not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We had an opportunity to look at the scenes from Srebrenica and Potocari in the course of your testimony. And those pictures were taken by a Dutch soldier. The film depicts a UN truck transporting the civilian population from the UNPROFOR base in Srebrenica to the base in Potocari. That starts at 14.55 and goes on for some 18 minutes. Do you remember all that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Why didn't you include all that into your clip book, video-clip book? Is there a special reason -- or, rather, the book of stills?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, to make it clear, I did not make the stills book. It was made prior to my coming to the OTP, so I am not sure of all the reasons that photographs were selected. I know often times the use of the book was for identifying people, and particularly these Bosnian Serb soldiers, officers, that were there. So when I was using this book during my investigation, it was to try to identify the -- the -- for me, usually, the police that were there along the road. As to why still photographs were not selected for this book, that is my assumption, as to why none were selected of that particular footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you recognise anybody who has testified here about the events that were unfolding at that time in the UNPROFOR bases in Srebrenica and Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And do you mean specifically from that footage or from any of the footage in Srebrenica and Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I mean that footage. Did any of those who could testify about the transport of Muslims from Srebrenica to Potocari actually testify here before this Tribunal, and did you recognise them in this particular footage? And then, after that, in any footage at all as you said it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that particular footage of the refugees coming into the UN base, no, I don't recognise any of the DutchBat soldiers, that any of them have testified here. Certainly later in the footage that you see in Potocari on the 12th and the 13th, you -- some of those I think you have already seen testify and will be testifying here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is a rather broad question. The book is loaded with people, many of whom have testified, so if she is going to be able to answer that completely, I think she would probably need to go through the book. But I am satisfied with the brief answer she gave. I don't know, but in order for it to be complete that would probably be the best way to do it. But, again, it's up to the General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I asked the witness that because she mentioned what footage was included. Could the Court please produce P624, page 9 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And let's now see and let's compare whether this footage is much more important than the footage depicting the arrival of the refugees from one UNPROFOR base at another UNPROFOR base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question: Is it more important to investigate only this still where we don't even see a proper date than the footage depicting refugees being transported from one UNPROFOR base to the other UNPROFOR base and also that latter footage depicts those who participated in these events and who could testify about these events. Is the latter more important than this one that we see now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, certainly, at the time, there were probably hundreds of statements taken from refugees that had been at the base, taken to the base, transferred out of Potocari. So all those statements is initially how the investigation started, then the question became more of who was involved in the -- the attack, the transfer, of the refugees. So the identities of the others became the question and became what was the next important step after many of the witness statements had already been taken of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the compilation that has been prepared for this trial, there is also an interview that was given in Potocari by General Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce P1008, page 42 in Serbian and English, page 57. This will be the footage of General Krstic giving an interview in Srebrenica. That's from 02.03.40.42.6 [as interpreted], that's the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now we can see both English and Serbian versions. And I'm reading. The General asks General Krstic: "What is your comment of the NATO against the Serbian army? All that is known that the Muslim from this former enclave were constantly attacking and inflicting losses on the Serbs where terrorist actions mostly attacking civilians." This is what Krstic answers: "The action of the NATO air force is puzzling on account of one single reason. They know that the bulk of the Dutch battalion troops have passed onto our territory and requested from us to guarantee their safety. I mean, that is indeed puzzling. We are not scared of the NATO air force. We are proceeding to the very end." My question is this: Did you or anybody from the OTP have an opportunity to interview a Dutch battalion soldier who had crossed to the Serbian side during the activities and did you try to investigate why they had done that? Is it true what General Krstic says here, that they sought protection from the Serbs in view of the fact that they had suffered losses and casualties when they were on the Muslim side? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's beyond the scope of direct. Nothing to do with her testimony analysing the statements and incidents in this case. And that particular objection, Your Honour, as you know is designed to target examinations, limit the massive time that's spent. That could have been a question for Mr. Ruez, who did the whole investigation, but this witness has been put on for a particular reason and that had nothing to do with the authentication of the video or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that this witness is capable to answer this question, if there is an answer to that. Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- certainly there have been many statements taken from DutchBat soldiers, and we certainly know that there were a number of them, as you saw in the Hotel Fontana footage, that were -- gave themselves up, basically, when their observation posts were overrun, and as you saw they were held as hostages in Hotel Fontana. That is my immediate recollection regarding this. I -- otherwise, I wouldn't really want to say more about any other -- I don't think I'm the appropriate person to answer that question the best. I think there will be some DutchBat soldiers coming up that can answer that better than I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I only asked the witness whether she knows if anybody of them had provided a statement, but since Mr. McCloskey suggested what the answer should be, I am not going to proceed with this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My next question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To be clear, I have no problem with the General asking questions on that. And, yes, Ms. Gallagher is, of course, capable of answering any questions on Srebrenica. And so I do not want to limit the scope of the General's questions. So I just want to make that -- be clear. I do believe in the principle of beyond the scope of direct, but that is not my call, and so I will -- but I have no problem with any of the rulings or the questions under them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise. During the examination-in-chief, this footage was shown with the references that I have mentioned, but let's not waste any more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On transcript page 6695, you said that the Muslim civilians had to travel 5 to 7 kilometres on foot from Srebrenica to where they were loaded off the buses and in the Muslim territory. Were you there? Were you on the spot? Did you measure how long the journey was from Srebrenica to the separation line between the territory under the control of the Serbs and the territory under the control of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we are talking about the footage of Tisca and Luka, when they were dropped off from the buses. As I have mentioned before, I have not been to this area between Tisca and Kladanj. I certainly have not specifically been to this area to measure it. I have looked in the map and that was my rough recollection was around 5 kilometres, but you know, I may be off a couple of kilometres on that one. It's my rough recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It is very important if you studied the matter from the drop-off point to the border of Republika Srpska, how far was that and how much of that was as an interspace, a no man's land as it were. You will remember the aerial photos that we saw. The last part of my sentence has been misinterpreted, probably due to the speed, so the interpreter did not arrive at -- to interpreting. How far is the place where the Muslims were dropped off in Republika Srpska to the border or the separation line between Republika Srpska and the Muslim-Croatian Federation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, my answer is the same. I don't know the exact number of kilometres. My rough recollection is still that it's around 5 kilometres, but that is my rough recollection. It's based off of looking at a map, not because I measured it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If it's indeed 5 kilometres from the drop-off point to the border of Republika Srpska, how far is it from the border of Republika Srpska to the place where the refugees were received on the other side by the Federation of Muslims and Croats or Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is still the same, that the -- the buffer area is still roughly about 5 kilometres, but I really -- I don't -- I can't give you any more information than that about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At the Prosecutor's request, you drew up the separation line. Could the buses enter the buffer area or not?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection from Colonel Boering's statement is that they were dropped off at the one side of no man's land and the people -- as he called it, and they then walked to -- through the no man's land, the buffer area, to the free territory. So my presumption is no, the buses could not enter into that buffer area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Let's go to my next question. We saw a wire fence in Tuzla in one of the photos, and that wire fence fenced off the area where the refugees were. Did you investigate why they had to be fenced off, or is it perhaps the case that that wired fence had been there even before the refugees arrived?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had not investigated the fence for the purposes of testifying for this video. I don't know if it was there prior or set up after or during. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you investigate why Muslims were forbidden to leave that area? As we saw in the footage, there was a sign there forbidding the Muslims to leave the area, do you know why that was the case? Thank you. I was not very clear in my question. We also saw a police car in the footage and the police were saying that they shouldn't leave the area. Did you have an opportunity later on to investigate why the refugees were not allowed to leave the area? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware from this footage that the Muslims were not allowed to leave the area. I don't think this part of the video had been subtitled, and, no, not for the purpose of testifying here did I investigate, if that is correct, why they were not allowed to leave the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce P1008, page 63 in English, and 47 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On the video footage that starts at 2 hours, 18 minutes, 20 seconds, and goes on until 2 hours, 18 minutes, and 30 seconds, that footage was taken at Tuzla airport. You can see a police car and you can hear the following messages coming from the police loud speaker. I am just going to read one part of the transcript. Here you can see that it says police on the right-hand side in English, and it says: "Exit from the perimeter of the airport at the main gate. There are about 3.000 refugees ...," and then unintelligible, "... they will be accommodated across southern municipalities. Any individual departure from this area is forbidden. "Notice: This is to inform all refugees from the area of Srebrenica that there will be an organised transportation by buses to ...," unintelligible, "... accommodation facilities and they will be provided medical attention." My first question is this: Did you investigate the reasons why the refugees were not allowed to leave the area where they were first taken in by the Muslims? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see from the transcript. I had certainly forgotten about this quote by the police in it, that they are not allowed to leave the area. No, I have not investigated or spoken with any of the refugees that were there at that time as to why they were not allowed to leave the area, not for the purposes of this testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did either you or anybody from the OTP investigate whether the refugees enjoyed the freedom of movement once they arrived in the Muslim territory? Was their accommodation in the municipalities to which they were subsequently transferred and they stay there voluntary or were they forced to go wherever they were told to go?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly in reading a number of statements from refugees that had arrived in Tuzla, my memory of these statements was they had no place to go. They were, you know, their homes had been in Srebrenica, they have been transferred there, I know they were in makeshift tents in the airport grounds for a while, while accommodations were being found. I don't recollect from these statements that I've read quite a while ago whether they were forced to stay there, allowed not to leave, I don't recall. What I recall is that many of them had no place to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. In your evidence yesterday, page 6994, when asked by Judge Nyambe: "Can you tell who the people are with the horses?" You said: "I don't know exactly who they are, but I believe these are Bosnian Serbs who are returning to the area or are returning to loot, to take the property that was left behind by the Muslims who left." My question is: Were you able to identify during your investigation who the people with the horses are and what they were doing in that film that Judge Nyambe asked you about? Did you try to determine that? If you didn't, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not try to determine who this -- the men were on the horses. What I recollect from various interviews and statements I've read is that locals from the area, Bosnian Serbs that used to live in the area, were coming back into the villages to loot and reclaim lands and houses and that there was a lot of looting that was going on during that time. And those are statements and interviews that had been done with Bosnian Serb police and officers that were there in July of 1995, but I do not know specifically who those men were with the horses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In any case, you did not investigate that so that any qualification attached to things we know nothing about is out of place.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than -- no, other than that the statements that were made in the interviews about people coming into the village and looting, no, nothing more. I cannot add anything more about the investigation of -- of those people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the Srebrenica video from 0.05.42 to 0.6.19. We see mortar fire there from Srebrenica in the vicinity of the UNPROFOR base.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Aleksandar. Can you tell us in which direction these grenades are fired?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe that is near the gas station on the more northern end of the village, so it -- it looks like it's -- like they're firing north but -- slightly north-west, but that is just a -- that's an estimate on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the case that on the footage before, fire was registered from the Bosnian Serb positions in that direction? Did you look at all of that footage and did you hear before this point any explosions or any fire directed at the mortar or the population gathering for demonstrations and protests?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you mean this same footage in the town of Srebrenica, the -- immediately before but part of this same footage?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry, and do you also mean the original raw footage versus the trial video, or what we've seen in the trial video?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know what the original raw foot shows because I didn't see it. I only saw the trial video during examination-in-chief where you can only see the fire from these mortars close to the petrol station. And nobody was firing on the population, otherwise they would not have been gathering, they would have scattered. Perhaps my next question will help you: Was there any attempt to identify the persons around the mortar because they are quite clearly visible on the film?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. To answer your first question, at least at that moment, no, I don't believe that we see any -- any incoming fire onto the people gathered there, not at that moment. A little bit later in this -- the person who made the -- who took this footage, there was some fire that came in a little bit later at some time after 1300 hours on the video. And in terms of identifying those individuals, I am not aware that the men in that -- that footage there were identified. Certainly, they were not identified by the person who made the video in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is it possible to identify from the film the persons who were firing the mortar near the petrol station around which Muslim civilians were gathering and listening to a speech? This mass of people, were they Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. As we know, there are Muslims that are gathered in Srebrenica before leaving the enclave. And yes, I'm sure some of them can be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you said there was no incoming fire before that from the Serbian side and there was some later on around 1300 hours, would it be fair to say that this mortar fire provoked the later fire you mentioned, and is it a textbook example how enemy fire is provoked and directed at the civilian population because the normal reaction to fire is to return fire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. She did not say there was no fire. Of course, she cannot say that. She wasn't there. She may have said that she didn't see any on the video, so that's a completely improper question. He can pose it as a hypothetical, if there was no fire, as it was not seen on the video, then. But he cannot say something that she did not say in the record because that would be improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness said: "To answer your first question, at least at that moment, no, I don't believe that we see any -- any incoming fire onto the people gathered there, not at that moment." Mr. Tolimir, if you take this formulation into account, you should rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. But the witness also said, I quote: "Perhaps a little later after 1300 hours there was fire." I don't know where, perhaps we can ask her. Was it fire against the civilians, was it shooting at the group of civilians who had gathered and demonstrated. I can ask that, but if Mr. McCloskey doesn't want me to ask that, I don't have to. But she said herself, "Perhaps a little later ...," that means she has a good recollection of the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you asked for an interpretation of casualties seen on the footage. Is this really the right witness to make such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since the witness was able to see both the raw footage and the selected footage, I asked whether the mortar fire from the petrol station had provoked any return of fire from the other side and was it a way to cause the other side to fire and cause massive casualties. She said herself there was fire later. I am asking when later, when the civilians had already dispersed or while they were still gathered there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your question was quite different. You said: "Is it a textbook example how enemy fire is provoked and directed at the civilian population because the normal reaction to fire is to return fire?" This is a question to get an interpretation of something what happened on the ground. I think you should ask people on the ground who have been taking part in these casualties, but I think this witness is not the proper witness to interpret what has been done on the ground or to be seen in the film. She is not a military expert. Please carry on and be careful with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Would you kindly tell us, did this -- was this fire after 1300 hours directed at civilians or had the civilians already dispersed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you see in the -- the raw footage is it's not in this immediate location. It looks like it's maybe a couple hundred metres away from the petrol station here. You see a big poof of smoke, and then you see people running. It's a little bit blurry. It's not easy to see. I think that's why it was not used in the trial video and that's what I was referring to, was -- and I can't remember the exact location -- excuse me, the exact time. I know it was after 1300 hours. I know it is in the -- the person who made -- who took this footage, it's in his statement as to exactly when that was, I can't recollect right now. And he did briefly describe that they had been fired upon and the people ran. And what you see on the trial videos, you don't catch the immediate fire, you will just see some of the people running afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That -- we do have that section that did not make it on the trial video, if that's of interest to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I am only interested in knowing whether the fire was directed at the civilians gathered around the petrol station or not. Perhaps this is something that persons, including the witness, who have seen the raw footage can tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not right at the people at the petrol station. It doesn't hit them. It looks like it's maybe a couple hundred metres away and you can't see if someone is hit, who is hit, or what is hit. It's a little bit hidden behind, I think, trees, and there are some structures there, some buildings there. So you can't see. The camera isn't able to zoom in close enough to see what actually was hit. So I don't know if anyone or who is hit, if they are civilians or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gallagher, for the answers you have provided. I am not going to press you on that. I am just asking for the record because I don't want the record to show that the fire was directed at the civilians who were gathered there. I had no other intention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have concluded my cross-examination, Mr. President. I thank everyone, especially Ms. Gallagher, who showed us the footage and the situations that we would need a lot of time to study properly, as she has already done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Mr. McCloskey, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, just a short -- a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On page 20 today, about 1 through 25 on that page -- sorry, that's the wrong location. On -- it was page 3 today, lines 1 through 3, the General asked you basically where did the BBC, Reuters, and the other compilations come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'd like to put on 65 ter 2935 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I am told that this is a document P331 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, all right. Yeah, it's an intercept so it may have the intercept operator's name on it. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's enough if that will not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's intercept number 569. So it's not the first one, it's that second one. That's 568, yeah. 569 is the one I would like to direct her attention to. And that's the first part of it we see in the English where it talks about a conversation between a journalist of the press centre of the so-called VRS Main Staff. And we need to flip to the second page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It says on that first page in the first conversation at 1435 hours, the journalist Vesna Stupar talks with an ITN representative, Neli Petrovic, and tells her that Lieutenant-Colonel Milutinovic had just called and informed her that he could offer her some exclusive recordings from Srebrenica. The price asked, which Vesna told her interlocutor, was the range of 25.000 to 30.000 Deutschmarks. Can you remind us who this Lieutenant-Colonel Milutinovic is, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in charge of the press for the VRS Main Staff, and you saw him, not through me, but on the Hotel Fontana footage. In the third meeting he is at the table during that negotiation, and if you haven't already, you will see footage of him also in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall reading this intercept among many in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this intercept before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think we have heard of WTN, you mentioned WTN, right? How about ITN, do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- yes, it's International Television Network.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, is this witness able to answer the questions of Mr. McCloskey that were not the subject of her inquiry, regardless of the fact that this footage was not taken from a foreign broadcasting company or camera crew? Mr. McCloskey is now asking about a different kind of material, something that the witness did not study.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't know that yet. Mr. McCloskey, what is your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The General clearly asked where all these journalists got this information, and he said BBC, Reuters. And we remember the witness saying earlier besides BBC, Reuters, there was WTN and other journalists. And I think she said that they -- she opined where they might have got them from the original sources when she was talking about which cameramen were at various places, Potocari, combat cameramen, she just testified about that. Now we see the head of the press of the Main Staff VRS press corps, who she has just told us were present in Potocari on the 12th, talking with ITN which is much like, as she has just explained, Reuters, WTN, Associated Press, and offering to sell, and if we get to that part, we'll see what they are wheeling and dealing over. Clearly this is the answer, in my view, to the General's question to her, earlier in the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. We are satisfied with that. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, just to go on, and we -- as we can see from this, this is not one of those intercepts that has each line. It's more of a synopsis intercept; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the synopsis goes on and says: "Explaining what were the recordings showing, Vesna says that there was a young man recorded walking around Srebrenica, the UN forces, the refugees leaving Srebrenica, and this was, as she said, all she managed to remember, while there were other interesting things to." Do those descriptions match any of the footage that we are talking about that was seen on the trial video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then there is another synopsis. It's in that same intercept. At 1520 hours, Lieutenant-Colonel Milutinovic is talking directly with someone named Vojo, and they are talking about offering the same material. And then it goes on to say: "Milutinovic says that in question, our VHS video tape recordings which are of very good quality, there are recordings of combat and the entry of the so-called VRS to Srebrenica." And then a conversation with the UN representatives and also a conversation with the representatives of Muslims in Srebrenica and lots of other things. Then in the end, it says that: "Milutinovic managed to reach an agreement on the sale of material for 25.000 Deutschmarks." And had you read -- do you recall reading this intercept at some point in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you think the information contained in it is reliable?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does that help in answer, in your view, the General's question about where all these news agencies got this material from?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where would that be?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly, Lieutenant-Colonel Milutinovic was one source.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Just one more. If we could go to 65 ter -- well, that other intercept is already in evidence, Mr. President. If we could go to 65 ter number 3099. I'm sorry, that's P320. It's also in evidence. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question. Sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. In line 8, in answer to Mr. McCloskey's question, you say -- he asked you: "Do you think the information contained in it is reliable," he's referring to an intercept. And you said: "Yes." How are you able to determine whether information in an intercept is reliable or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly know of an example that supports this of other footage. In fact, it involves the Petrovic footage that had been -- had been sold and had been the custody of -- or part of it had been in the custody of the VRS and Lieutenant Milutinovic. So I know that he has been involved in -- in releasing and selling video footage at other times, and I think there is also another intercept regarding this. And so in particular to this situation, I think he has been -- we've shown to be involved in -- it corroborates that he has sold other footage. And, otherwise, in terms of the intercepts they -- we've seen through the course of the investigation, that they have been corroborated by many means and have not been shown to be -- or, I should say, they have been shown to be true and accurate and authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. You mention you thought there might -- that there was another intercept on that topic, and so let's go to this one which is CSV. And can you take a look at it and tell us if you recall this one and could this be something that you have -- were thinking of in that last answer or not? And I will just go over it just very briefly. I don't want to read the whole thing, but we see that it's 20 July and that's it's between someone from the aggressor's army which, since it's a Muslim intercept, the aggressor's army would be who?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then someone that they couldn't hear but that they thought, as it says, from a news organisation. And it says: "X: We're here in Han Pijesak, there is material, these talks and the conclusions of the talks and the departure of the two Muslims who negotiated with General Mladic and what was agreed for 1000 hours tomorrow. The wounded and ill will start off. The wounded and ill are going to Sarajevo at 1400 hours ..." It goes on and talks about the people that will be leaving. And then it says, X again: "The shot shows General Mladic, General Tolimir, the arrival of two Muslims with a white flag at the UNPROFOR base where the talks were held, then the UN representatives, the two Muslims, the Serbian officers and the generals. The talks, the conclusion of the talks, the salutes, he gives them cigarettes and three bottles of wine and the handshake and departure." Does that description, the two Muslims, the white flag, Mladic, Tolimir, et cetera, recall anything from any -- any tape that has been used in this case and that was part of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it seems clearly it's from the negotiations that -- regarding Zepa, that happened at Boksanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And if you glance through the rest of it, it mentioned Colonel Dudnjik, the commander of the Ukrainian Battalion, was he seen in that segment you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's also in that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It says at the bottom of the English for X to come to Belgrade so you can see its together, sign the contract, and edit the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, during this witness's testimony we have not seen any footage of Zepa, only of Srebrenica. I don't know why this transcript of intercepts is being introduced through her. She never mentioned anything about either the intercepts or anything that had happened in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it is clear what Mr. McCloskey is doing. He wants to show how video material was obtained. And we have now a problem, because we are over time now. Perhaps you can explain, Mr. McCloskey, just in brief what is the purpose of this and then we must break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. As I think everyone will recall, the video footage of the Zepa negotiations with General, in quote, negotiations with General Tolimir, Mladic, Dudnjik, the wine, Zepa, Boksanica, as just confirmed by the witness. And that is in evidence. It's part of the same collection that the Court has seen. It's very similar to the Srebrenica collection, the same kind of material, so it goes precisely to the question raised by General Tolimir and it was a good question: Where did the news organisations get this stuff from. And we had one answer for Srebrenica, now we have another answer for Zepa. It's a good question and this is the simple answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have any problem with that, but we have to break now and we will resume five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have P00334 up. Another intercept that's in evidence. It's from the CSB. It's a Muslim intercept, and I'll just briefly go over it as we are waiting for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's -- the English translation says 12 May, 1995, but if we believe that is a typo, actually, a typo in the original that can be sorted out, if you look at all the -- I believe, if you look at all the originals. But in any event, let's just look at the substance of that right now. It's between -- a conversation between a journalist and certain Michael, and they couldn't hear Michael, so it's just a one-sided conversation. And it says: "Morale is lifted, as they say, by three octaves. "You see, I know, they are probably listening to us. We should not take a break so we can finish with Gorazde." It goes on and says: "I would like to ask you, since we have already given film, and it will be broadcast perhaps tonight on some television stations. Our entrance into Srebrenica and that bombing, so give me a call and let me know how it went. We gave of Mladic walking through Srebrenica and looking around town. We gave it to the ITN and that is a TV agency that will sell it to the others." Does that help answer the General's question in -- in your view is this reliable?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does answer the question, and I do believe it's reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the end it says not "to the others" but "to the other users." It is not a big difference, just for the clarity of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let me just have one more up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that is 65 ter 3484. This is a -- not yet in evidence, it's a series of three intercepts. The one I am interested in is number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Gajic. Mr. Gajic? No interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would kindly ask Mr. McCloskey to slow down a little. Mr. McCloskey actually speaks much faster than the interpreters can follow. It's very difficult to follow in two different languages because the transcript is about three or four lines slower than his actual words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I will -- I feel like I'm talking in slow motion, but I can try to slow it down even more. I know it's especially difficult when reading. And this, as I mentioned, is a series of -- it's a print-out of three intercepts, and I am interested in the one that is number 748. Its 19 July at 2255 hours. And for some reason we were not -- we did not get the English translation in e-court, but I have it, it's short. And I'll just, if that's okay, read it slow. It's number 748. It's 19 July, 2255 hours. Yeah, it's that one in the middle. Perhaps you could blow it up one more time because it's a short one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It says a conversation between Milovanovic, and a person, X, who is inaudible. Now, any idea who this Milovanovic might be in your view and memory?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my immediate response is it's General Milovanovic, Chief of Staff of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And X is not audible, so again it's one of these where all they have is Milovanovic, and it says, as we can read it: "Yes, hello. Yes, yes. For himself, Radul has just called me." Any idea who Radul is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "Listen, I will give it to AP, it will pay me 25, and I don't know what he will do." Then he says: "That's right, that's correct. I don't know. I am not interested in these Palvi. Tomorrow at 0600 hours, I am heading out to the site." Then he goes on to say: "Well, the boss told me to take nothing under 50.000 German marks for tomorrow's work." He goes on to say: "It is all for 50 except for the one of this evening. "All right. Fifty is good. Yes. In the next three days until the wounded civilians and soldiers come out and are in Zepa." And then he goes on to say: "The same cameraman, everything is the same." Then he says: "There is no other crew there. The boss ordered General Tolimir that only one camera can go in. Call again. Bye." Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually have not seen this intercept before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any opinion on what -- well, we can see the mention of Zepa here. Does that reference to Zepa have any -- is there any information in that that you can connect to the case, the investigation at all, if we look at the date of 19 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. We know that the meeting at Boksanica happened on July 19th, that General Tolimir and General Mladic and Zepa representatives were at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to know whether this witness is being examined as an expert who provides an opinion about the events which were not presented here, either during the trial or in the examination-in-chief, or maybe the goal of this examination is different. The Prosecutor has just invited the witness to share her opinion with us. I don't mind the witness talking about Zepa, but then I should also be given the right to take that matter further. The issue of Zepa was mentioned neither in the examination-in-chief nor in my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. Tolimir, insofar as this witness was not asked about Zepa. This is true. And, Mr. McCloskey, you should be careful with questioning the witness about the situation on the ground. I take it that you are -- want to show how the videos of different situations and events have been obtained. This is, indeed, a correct course of questioning because you, personally, were asking, Mr. Tolimir -- the witness about her knowledge how these videos were produced and obtained by the OTP. The chain of custody and the original source are, as I understand it, the background of your questioning. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and that is correct, Mr. President. And that's the principle reason I am putting this intercept up, as we can see, and you'll soon see from my last couple of questions. There is also, in release to that, I think Judge Nyambe brought up the question of intercept authenticity of backing up this topic of films and camera crews. And the witness's answer in that provided brief explanations of why she thought an intercept was authentic and reliable, and so because of that concern, I was asking her those questions to tie this intercept as relevant and authentic before I got to the main point, which we are almost there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the bottom we see: "There is no other crew there. The boss ordered General Tolimir that only one camera can go in." Now, has there been any footage that we have had and used in this case of video footage in the town of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Footage of inside the town of Zepa in July of 1995 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- other than -- well, excuse me, we do have footage of inside the town of Zepa in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you recall if General Tolimir can be seen in that footage?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I think I can leave it at that, Mr. President, in terms of that. I would offer that intercept into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I -- the witness said she hasn't seen this intercept before. She can't tell anything about the content and the authenticity of this intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's my view that the key to the authenticity of the intercept, one of the keys is that the witness has testified that German marks are being sold for video. This backs that up. She is also able to establish that, yes, in fact, there was a camera crew in Zepa, and this is backed up by this intercept. This idea that -- or this, and this may not be the right place for this, but the idea that a witness has never seen something really, in my view, is -- is one consideration you should have in determining whether something is admissible but not the only. If the witness's testimony on a point that is being contradicted by something the opposing party brings out is supported by a document, that document, in my view, should be something the Court can see. And that's as true for the Defence side as it is the Prosecution side. And so because we, you know, I don't think you want to see another intercept operator. So the substance of this backs up what she has been saying in response to General Tolimir's question about where this material came from and the Judge's question on is it authentic, because it shows that there is a video -- that they are talking about a video crew in Zepa. So that is something I will hope you will consider in your authenticity -- or in your admissibility decision. But, as I hope you will for the Defence as well, because they have brought up documents sometimes that have the same issue, and we will get together with them to determine if there is any such things like that and so their documents can get in as well, but I think it's very important. The substance of a document may be just as important to the witness's testimony, whether or not that witness has ever seen the document. I don't believe in just willy-nilly just bringing documents in. That is a frightening aspect, and I don't want to do that. But I do want, especially since we've had concern about the number of -- she said there were a number of intercepts that helped deal with this issues. And this is one of those. And I have a Judge -- Judge Nyambe is concerned about authenticity of intercepts relating to video, and so that's another reason why I bring this intercept in. So that's -- I guess that's all I have to say on it, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation and clarification of your position. Mr. Tolimir, do you want to comment? What is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the position of the Defence on the intercepts is well known. If this witness has not seen a document and she only saw similar documents, you can't actually testify about a person walking on two legs because you saw another person walking on two legs. I don't think it's acceptable for documents to be admitted through this witness. And we cannot bring Muslim officers here to talk about documents drafted by them, so we cannot reciprocate. If a document may be admitted through a witness about Srebrenica, which were not actually subject of her investigation and research, then you, please, alert me to that fact and I will feel free to introduce documents of any kind through this witness which were not previously on the subject of my cross-examination. And I will have them admitted, or at least ask for their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have now the position of the parties on the record. The Chamber will postpone its decision thereon and we come back to that later. Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That was the last intercept that I had. So I also have before me, and it doesn't have a 65 ter number, but it was the subject of the General Tolimir's question, and that is the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- we can. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But now we know to whom you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In fact, it's a very short statement, and if I could very -- I'll slowly read the part that has to the with the part of the questioning General Tolimir made, and we should probably go into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have to thank you for your attendance here, Ms. Gallagher. You are free now to return to your normal work, no restrictions any longer. Thank you very much. And you are free now to leave the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I believe Mr. Janc and Mr. Vanderpuye are ready to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. Before we continue, could I please ask you -- or, rather, suggest that the recording that was erroneously shown be marked for identification, and then when he has another opportunity to show it maybe we can discuss that recording as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You mean the last footage, video footage we have just seen?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The last footage we saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, the last footage we saw was part of the trial video, the famous gas station mortar crew. And we can, I know, find the other part relatively quickly to show it. So at first chance, we can do that for the General, and I think that's fair enough, since it was a question that he brought up that I was trying to respond to and he's still interested. So I know we can get that, it won't be long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, we should mark this -- in my understanding, that was part of the raw material of the video and some parts of that were taken into the trial video. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Actually, that is correct, Mr. President. It -- we can mark that separately. As far as I could tell, everything that we saw was played on the trial video but we were playing it from a different tape, so we can -- we should give it another number. Let me get some help from Ms. -- I think the Registrar can give it the appropriate number, that that would be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video clip, Your Honours, played with 65 ter 01382 will be assigned Exhibit P01301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we welcome Mr. Vanderpuye and the next witness shall be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President. I believe on page 45, line 1, the number was wrongly recorded because it appears like this exhibit number is P101.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the purposes of the record, Your Honours, I will repeat the number. The video clip played with 65 ter 01382 will be assigned P01301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we have it on the record. Welcome, Mr. Janc, back to the courtroom. May I remind you that the information you made at the beginning of your testimony on the 15th of April this year, to tell the truth, still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, Mr. Vanderpuye has concluded his direct examination on the 23rd of September, 2010, and now Mr. Tolimir is prepared to start with his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll welcome Mr. Janc, and I have a couple of questions about his earlier testimony. First of all, when you described in examination-in-chief your preparations for giving evidence, on page 5721, line 17 through 21, you said, I quote: "I familiarised myself with the information about the way the OTP got hold of these videos and other material, and I also took into account issues of authenticity in order to prepare for my testimony." I hope I quoted you correctly. Do you agree with this quotation? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that when preparing for giving evidence you only studied the documentation of the OTP, but you did not participate in any way in collecting the material and establishing its authenticity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I studied the documentation of the OTP and also trying to find facts regarding the -- establishing the authenticity, going through the OTP documents. So those were, I would say, combined issues, so -- which I examined together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. To be quite precise, did you personally conduct any interview with any person that delivered to the OTP any material that was introduced through you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you then give us your point of view about the authenticity of the material and how this authenticity was determined by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The videos which we obtained from different sources, for example, we interviewed these individuals, so that was done by my colleagues, not personally by me. And these individuals have told us how did they obtain or how did they come across this material. On the other hand, some of the material, as you also know, was seized from the premises of different individuals, mainly in Serbia, and examining the documentation on the seizure itself, this was one source of getting information of the -- on the authenticity of this material. On the other hand, examining these videos, we have established that -- that several other similar videos already exist in OTP's possession which were obtained before from other different sources, for example, and were also corroborated in these ways. So then the third thing of authenticity was the content on the videos itself. You can -- one can clearly establish going -- reviewing these videos that what is going on is in line with the ongoing investigation -- with the investigation which was done and in line with the documents and the different information which was obtained by the OTP throughout the years. So there are different means how to authenticate these videos, and I was going through these steps in order to authenticate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, based on studying this documentation, whether OTP staff used experts or studied in any other way some of the material that was used here in the last round of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware that -- if any of these videos were ever examined by any of the experts. So I don't have this information, so I would say they were not examined by any of the experts. But no, they were not. I don't have any such reports, so they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since part of the material was obtained by buying it for very large amounts, you mentioned 200.000 Euros, was such material checked for possible editing? Because these things are impossible to identify when you study the cuts in the movie. Was this material given to any experts to investigate?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I have to correct you here, because I haven't testified that the OTP bought this video for 200.000 Euros. In information -- actually, a declaration by the OTP investigator, Tore Soldal. It's clearly written that that was the amount requested by the provider of this video initially, and OTP refused to pay for this video. And later on, this individual gave up and provided the OTP this video free of charge. So the OTP hasn't paid any money for this video. Of course, the authenticity was an issue for the OTP all the time regarding this video, and that's why a lot of interviews, first of all, have been conducted with different individuals, and they have basically confirmed the authenticity for the OTP. On the other hand, as you have seen here, represented on the several images and also presentation of the crime scene itself, and through that, the OTP independently confirmed that what can be seen on the video is, indeed, taking place at that spot. So, regarding the editing, yes, we can see on this video several edits and the OTP hasn't approached any expert to look closely on these additions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely what I wanted to know, and I am satisfied with your answer. I stand corrected that Tore Soldal said that this money was never paid, that some money was turned over for that person to move to a different territory later. Anyway, on this film with several interruptions, you said expertise was never required, but did you wonder at these interruptions in the film because it is mentioned both in the film itself and in the statement that this filming was commissioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning to you and Your Honours and everyone. I apologise for the interruption, but it seems to me that the question is not clear as to which film we are talking about. I think what we are talking about is Skorpions video. But there were, I think, seven videos that were introduced through Mr. Janc or clips of videos through Mr. Janc. So if General Tolimir could be more specific in the question, I think it would be helpful, at least in terms of clarifying the record, as we go along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, can you indicate which video you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, and thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. I was talking about what you mentioned -- in fact, what the witness mentioned, and he talked about the killings in Trnovo, and it's good for the record to say whether there was any editing and interruptions on this film. And if the witness could enlighten us about that, considering that no expertise was ever done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I already said, there are interruptions on this video. You can see them, and the OTP considered them and, of course, we tried to find out if there is any -- if there are any additional footages of these same incidents somewhere else. And that's why we interviewed several individuals, and they all confirmed that that's the entire video as it was filmed at the time. And since it was confirmed through several witnesses, we considered it as authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
