utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for that answer. My question was: Is there any additional material or footage that corroborate the authenticity of that film from Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP is not aware or is not in possession of any other footage which would corroborate this video. In relation to additional material, I would -- I would say the statements of the participants, several of them which were obtained by the OTP through interviews or through requests to the authorities of the Republic of Serbia, this is the additional material we have on this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we have already started on the subject of the killings in Trnovo, let's stay on it for a while.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see P1004, page 5 in e-court. It concerns the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And this was introduced into evidence through you and your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a small correction, P104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We see this map admitted in the last round of your testimony. Can you tell us whether these executions in Trnovo took place in the area of the Drina Corps or in the area of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps at its -- on its western boundary, as we see on this map where Trnovo is marked.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These killings took place in Trnovo, which you can see here on the map, which is south of Sarajevo, a few kilometres south of Sarajevo, and this is area of Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In your evidence in chief, on page 5802, line 21, you estimated that Trnovo is some 200 kilometres away from Srebrenica. Based on that distance and based on this map, isn't it clear that Trnovo is outside the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you. This area is outside the Drina Corps area of responsibility. It is inside the Sarajevo Romanija Corps AOR, area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We are still talking about information concerning the executions of these six persons in Trnovo. I won't mention their names. Did you personally investigate how they ended up in Trnovo, which is 200 kilometres away from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally, but several steps towards this -- this, regarding this issue have been done by the other members of the OTP investigators, my colleagues. And there is a statement of one of the individuals who was interviewed who says that these individuals, not only this also, but some other individuals, were brought from the area of Srebrenica, after the fall of Srebrenica, by buses and trucks to Trnovo area. These buses and trucks were going up and down several times and were bringing the -- the men from Srebrenica down to this area, and these six individuals, those were the last group of those transported down from Srebrenica and were subsequently killed there. Apart from that, I also examined the records on these individuals which we have -- which the OTP has in the possession. So -- and initially, the ICMP missing list and ICRC missing list, they both tell me that these six individuals are reported or have been reported as missing after the fall of Srebrenica. In addition, as I also testified here, we obtained four statements from the relatives of four of those individuals, and they all confirmed to the OTP that those were the individuals who left Srebrenica after its fall. And one of them, who we interviewed, was brother of one who we see killed, and they left Potocari -- sorry, Srebrenica, together through the woods towards Kladanj, and at one point they just miss each other -- missed each other in the woods, and he has never seen him again. So these were the steps I have taken in order to corroborate, these are indeed Srebrenica-related victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This is something new, at least for me. You're saying the buses and lorries transported people from Srebrenica to Trnovo; am I right? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is according to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- one of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and this is according to one of the individuals the OTP interviewed. I know his name, but I'm not sure if I can state that in public session, but I'm willing to provide you with the name of this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I am not interested in the name. I am interested in the number of people. And if those people were transported by buses and lorries, where are these people? Were their remains found in the locations around Trnovo, and if they were found around Trnovo, were they then returned to the places where their graves were found?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, and this was also my concern when I read this statement, and still is my concern when I read this statement. And -- because he says that the trips -- there were several trips with lorries and buses -- or lorries and truck and -- sorry, trucks and buses and buses or trucks to this area, and this was one of the last groups which was taken down there. And this is, indeed, the only group of individuals, I would say Srebrenica-related individuals which were so far found and identified in this area. So we don't have any additional graves, additional bodies found in this area which are related to Srebrenica events. And as you know, the exhumations are still ongoing process in Bosnia, and not all of the individuals who were already found and identified, and I don't exclude the possibility that in the future there might be additional individuals found in this area buried or on the surface or somewhere, which will be confirmed that they are the individuals which this person was talking us about. So there is a possibility that there is few more of them there, but, so far, we have only these six individuals identified and found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I am not going to disclose the person's name in open session, but let me ask you: Has he been asked to testify before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am almost sure he is not on a witness list in this case, but if he was ever called to testify in any other cases, I would need to check that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And since we are talking about just one witness who allegedly saw buses going backwards and forwards, I suppose they must have been transporting a lot of people, was the authenticity of his statement checked in any way? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OTP tried to obtain -- to obtain more corroborating statements in relation to the same issue; mainly, how and how many individuals were brought from Srebrenica area to this area, if at all any. But we have confirmation already that some of them, these six individuals, were brought down there. And unfortunately the only individual who told us about how they were brought down there was this person who I am talking about. We all, of course, asked all individuals which we interviewed in relation to this same issue these same questions, but they simply haven't told us any significant information. They haven't knew -- they haven't known this information or they simply said they cannot remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In your previous answer, you said that you assumed that those who were transported from Srebrenica to Trnovo would eventually be discovered. Where do you expect to find their remains? Do you think that they will be found in Trnovo or in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. This would be speculation, because they can be brought down there, and at some point in time, for unknown reason to us, brought back to Srebrenica. So they can be found on either place throughout the Bosnia, I would say, because it's not easy to say just, based on the fact -- on the information we are aware of now where those individuals would be buried if they were killed, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether the buses and lorries that the witness testified about, the one who allegedly saw those buses, did they also carry the six persons who were executed in -- at the location in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were part of the -- of the group which was transported down from Srebrenica area to Trnovo, and this was the last group of people transported to this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that national courts have tried those who are considered responsible for the killings in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can be a little bit more clear. I don't know now the national courts -- at what time, actually?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that national courts in the territory of the former Yugoslavia have tried those individuals who had admitted responsibility for the killing of the six persons in Trnovo that you are talking about? They have admitted their guilt and they were charged and tried.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Now I know what you are talking about. Yes, they were arrested and tried and convicted in the Republic of Serbia in Belgrade, and they were arrested in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I didn't understand you properly when you say that they were arrested, and then the rest of the sentence I didn't understand because the interpretation was poor.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat. These individuals who committed this crime were arrested in Serbia, I mean the Republic of Serbia in 2005, and then they were put on a trial, and they were convicted, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber whether this Tribunal has received documents from the trials of those persons who were held responsible for the crimes in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This Tribunal, actually, the OTP is in possession, I would say, of all the -- or most, I would say, most of the documentation which is related to the prosecution of these individuals, from their initial statements to the prosecutor, their trial testimonies, the trial itself, and the judgements. The OTP is in possession of this documentation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you study that documentation before you came here to testify? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I studied this documentation already before I came to testify, and I also prepared and read some of the material in preparation for this trial, but I have to admit that I haven't read everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you at least read the statements of the participants in the killings of those six people in Trnovo that you're testifying about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I am sure I read these statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you're sure that you read the statements, do you remember any of the statements describing the place where those bodies were found, where that place is, and how far it is from Srebrenica? Do you remember any of that from those statements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the top of my head, but if you show me, probably I will remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have the right to testify, but let me ask you this: The person who arrested them, you say that they had gone to attempt the breakthrough, according to their families, that's what you told us. You said that their families knew that they joined the column that we went in the direction of Susnjari and further on, and then you said that they were brought in, and the witnesses, whom we heard here at this trial, told us how they had come in contact with them. Do you know anything about the link between the Skorpions and those who were killed in Trnovo? How did the Skorpions get in contact with them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The clear answer to this is unfortunately not known to the OTP, as yet. So the only information and what kind of information the OTP has on this issue is what I testified about, how these individuals were most probably brought from Srebrenica area to the Trnovo, but how they were arrested or captured, when, on the way through the woods, that information is not known to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber that tried those persons in Belgrade, did they know at what point, at what location did they come in contact with the persons who were killed in Trnovo? Is it perhaps known from the documentation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, since you don't remember, I will not belabour the matter, but I thought that you studied everything thoroughly. But let me ask you something, this: On transcript, page 5085 [as interpreted], lines 25, through page 5086 [as interpreted], line 3, you spoke about the Skorpion deployment, and you said the following: "They were deployed --" or, rather, "there was an order of the 10th of July, 1995, signed by the then deputy minister of the interior, Tomo Kovac, for these units to be deployed in Srebrenica in order to assist in the operation that was going on in the Srebrenica enclave." Do you remember that you stated this and that a document was admitted through you on that occasion and that document is number P1025.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce P1025. Let's see if the witness remembers what he's stated about the Skorpions and why they are being included in the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm. I do remember saying that, but the document we can see on the screen right now is not the one I have been referring to. That must be a different one. And if I may so, when we are on this document which is on the screen, I have -- I was given a task to check how the OTP obtained this document, and I needed to check that and found out that this was seized in June/July 2003 by the OTP team who has made a visit to the public security centre, at that time Srpsko Sarajevo at Pale, and searched their archive and that's where this document was obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There are two things. First it -- I think it's at page 58, lines 8 through 9, there is a reference to the witness's prior testimony. And the transcript records that reference incorrectly as 5085 and 5086. It's actually 5805 through 5806. And the second relates to the scope of the question that General Tolimir has just put to the witness concerning the reasons why the Skorpions are part of the indictment, which I think is objectionable because it's outside of the ken of witness's knowledge. He can certainly testify as to circumstances of fact that support the allegations that are contained in the indictment, but as for the reasons that it's charged, I think that goes beyond the scope of his direct examination and, in fact, really the purpose of his testimony altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The problem is that your correction related to the page numbers is again not recorded. Please repeat that to have it clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The correction to the question should be that the reference 5085 through 5086 of the witness's prior testimony in the transcript should be pages 5805 through page 5806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And in relation to your concern about the question and the reasons for including it into the indictment, I would agree with your position but the witness has given his answer in the way he can give it. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Let's ask the witness exactly what he spoke about and what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The witness said that Tomo Kovac had issued an order on deploying Skorpions to Srebrenica; is that correct? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Court please produce 1D289. Thank you. Can I see 1D289. Thank you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there is a problem with the number again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If we have a problem, the document is here, maybe we can show it on the ELMO. In the meantime while the e-court is busy finding the document, maybe after the break we can solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, did you see this document and did you base your statement on that document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document is not on e-court, as I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: -- when you mentioned Tomo Kovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you are talking now about this document from 10th of July, 1995, the Tomo Kovac document, that's the document I have seen and I have been referring to, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I said the document is not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. Yes, yes, I am talking about that. Thank you. I am talking about this document. And after the break, we will display it since we have it here. If its not in e-court, we will display it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's a good proposal. We should have the second break now and the problem with the document will be resolved during the break. We will resume five minutes before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You said that a document dated 10 July was admitted through you. Is it the document we see on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it admitted because of this item 2: "The unit shall consist of the 2nd Special Police Detachment from Sekovici, the 1st Company of the PJP Zvornik SJB, a mixed company of joint RSK, Serbian and RS MUP forces, and a company from the training camp on Jahorina"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you give us the number of the document? We need it on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, 1D289.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I was asking because before the break we were not sure if that is the correct number, now it's clear. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's correct and the witness confirmed it was admitted through him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We've just read paragraph 2. Is there any reference to the Skorpions there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly to Skorpions, but to Serbian MUP. This is minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia, and part of which the Skorpion unit was, and that can be established through a document from 1st of July we've seen on our screen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we go back to that document, was this document dated 10 July sent by the Minister of Interior Kovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is his type-signed signature down there, but we can see it was not signed by him because we have a word "for" if front of the signature, and this is not his signature, and I know that from the fact that I read Kovac, his statement, and he was quite clear that this was not his signature that it was signature of duty operations officer or something like that, the Ministry of Interior office in Sarajevo at that time, and it was signed for him by this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, which is said to have been signed by someone else on behalf of Tomo Kovac and sent to these addresses as an order, is there a single word to the effect that the Skorpions are being sent to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no single word about the Skorpions -- Skorpion unit itself, but Skorpions were part of the Serbian MUP which was at the Trnovo battle-field at the time, or Sarajevo front, which is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We'll now see that other document which was on the screen before this, which you say is the basis for your assertion that the Skorpions were part of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I tender this document, and then I would like to see in e-court the document that the witness asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document, Your Honours, under document ID 1D00289 will be assigned Exhibit D00129.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now be shown the document he asked for, and that's P1025. Thank you. We see the document that the witness asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Tell us, on the basis of what do you claim that the Skorpions were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First, I think the question misstates fundamentally the witness's testimony, both on direct and cross-examination. And second of all, I think we can clarify this issue as a matter of position of the Prosecution, which is that the presence of the Skorpions in Srebrenica is not established by this document, nor is it established by the 10 July document. And we are not claiming that that as a matter of fact as yet in this case, and so I don't see that there is any basis for the question. But aside from the position of the Prosecution, I think it's readily apparent from the documents that General Tolimir is using that that is not an assertion that arises from it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If what the Prosecutor says is correct, then I do not need to ask anymore questions on this document. I called it up in e-court because the witness wanted it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness can answer the question: On the basis of what do you claim that the Skorpions were in Srebrenica? That was the question of Mr. Tolimir, I think, if you are able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I will clarify a little bit. Based on the document we have seen before, or based on that order, the Skorpion unit was ordered to go to Srebrenica. And it doesn't really mean that they went there, so they were just ordered to go there. And so far the Prosecution, I think, does not have any evidence that they were, indeed, in that area. And why we -- we -- why I say that Skorpions were referred as MUP Serbia is because of the paragraph 1 of this document, which we have in front of us from 1st of July, 1995. What it says, the second sentence, it starts: The combat group included certain platoons, and we have two platoons from the Kaman detachment, Plavi, and Skorpion, and then we have in brackets (Serbian MUP). And that's why these two documents are related, and that's why I claim that Skorpion unit was part of the Serbian MUP. Not only based on documents -- not only based on these documents, also based on the statement of the witnesses which we interviewed, and they all confirmed that they were part of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether this reference in the brackets, Serbian MUP, behind Skorpions, could be a mistake? Maybe what was meant was the MUP was Republika Srpska. Sorry, the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I'll ask my question can again: The author of this document, did he perhaps mean the MUP of Serbian Krajina but failed to write that exactly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, the writer of this report, Ljubisa Borovcanin, I think was quite right here because at that time the Skorpion unit was representing the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia at that time. And we can see -- we have seen from the order from 10th of July that there is distinction between those two units, MUP of the Republic of Srpska Krajina and MUP of the Republic of Serbia. So these are two units. And I am sure that Ljubisa Borovcanin was referring to the Skorpions in this document as a member of the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see in e-court 1D129, which just got an exhibit number. D129. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let us look again at paragraph 2 that we read a moment ago: "The unit shall consist of the 2nd Special Police Detachment from Sekovici, the 1st Company of the Special Police Unit from the Zvornik public security station, a mixed company of the joint Republic of Serbian Krajina, Serbian and RS MUP forces, and a company from the training camp on Jahorina." Now, based on what I've read, my question is: Is it clear from Tomo Kovac's order that the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina is separated from the MUP of Republika Srpska and the MUP of Serbia and that's why they are called joint forces?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That's clear from this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean, then, that the forces of the so-called Skorpions belonged to the MUP of the Serbian Krajina, not the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your concern, now, because -- I mean, previous document we don't have reference to the Republic of Serbian Krajina MUP but only to Serbian MUP, and one can conclude that under Serbian MUP in the document from 1st of July, they covered everything, both from the RSK to the Serbian MUP. But still, regardless of that fact, based on the statements from different individuals which we interviewed, it was made quite clear from their side that Skorpions, at that time, were there under the umbrella of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. So that's why I am testifying here today that Skorpion unit at that time was under the responsibility of the Republic of Serbia MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago you said, "one could conclude." Are you assuming or inferring or concluding?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am concluding that that's the fact based on all documents, if you complete -- if you put all the information we have on this unit together, I can conclude that they were under the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In this communication that we see, in paragraph 2, signed by somebody on behalf of Tomo Kovac, does it say, "A mixed company of the joint RSK MUP," and that means the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the document speaks for itself, and a joint unit at that time would be -- would consist of all those three MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said it included the forces of all the three MUPs, but here it says clearly a mixed company, specifying exactly how many units: "A mixed company of the joint RSK," separated by a comma, "Serbian and RS MUP forces and a company from the training camp on Jahorina." Does that mean that in these joint forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina there could have been Skorpions as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think the witness has already answered the question. The document, in fact, does speak for itself. What the General is proposing is a rather strained interpretation of what the document plainly reads, which is that: "A mixed company of joint RSK Serbian and RS MUP forces and a company from the training camp at Jahorina." It does not refer to a mixed force within the RSK forces, as the General is suggesting. It refers to a mixed force comprising those three elements and an element from a training camp at Jahorina. It's plain on its face, and I don't see that we are making a point or making any headway with repeated references to a rather contrived interpretation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think everybody can read the document, indeed. And now you provided Mr. Tolimir with an answer to the question put to the witness. But, indeed, we have received an answer by the witness about his understanding of this document. Do you want to add something, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If a mixed company is really joint, like the Prosecutor says, including a unit from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, would it then be logical that the Skorpions would be subordinate to the Republic of Serbian Krajina force because it is from another state, another country?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just repeat again that based on information the OTP has, is that the Skorpion unit was under the umbrella of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. So we have no indication, no information, that they were, at that time, under the Republic of Serbian Krajina MUP. So that's why I concluded and stated that they were under their authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that in your prior evidence you said that these Skorpions hailed from Vukovar, which is the Republic of Croatia, at the time it was the Republic of Serbian Krajina; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember testifying about that, and I still stand by my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If that's the Republic of Serbian Krajina, is it then logical that part of the units of the RSK would be subordinated to the MUP of Serbia rather than to their own MUP of the RSK, as Tomo Kovac writes here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logical or not, in wartime a lot of things are possible, and according to information and what I testified about is that at that time Skorpion unit was sent to Trnovo battle-field by the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. At previous occasions, they were in Bosnia. When they were deployed in Bosnia, they were under the Republic of Serbian Krajina at that time, but during the Trnovo battle-field operation, they were under the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but that's what you were saying. Now, tell me what's the name of that unit of that Republic of Serbian Krajina MUP which was part of this joint force? Did you find out which unit was that and who was its commander because Tomo Kovac is, by virtue of this order, sending that unit to Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have recollection about it right now, but I think that I came across information, who would those be, but I cannot be -- I cannot give you an exact answer right now. I think I would need to check -- re-check Tomo Kovac's statement again to see what he told us about these units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just with respect to the last question, there is a reference at page 69, line 17 -- 16 and 17 where General Tolimir talks about Tomo Kovac, and by virtue of that order, he says sending that unit to Trnovo. In fact, the document suggests that the unit, at least according to General Tolimir's position so far, was sent to Srebrenica. This is the 10 July 1995 document, so the witness's answer -- so either the question should be put back to the witness or the witness's answer should be interpreted in that context. I believe it was just a misstatement rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If a unit outside of the MUP is coming to join the MUP, is it then logical that the minister of the interior, as was the case here, should send it. And we read here: "Part of the forces involved in the Sarajevo theater of war," that includes Trnovo, "is sent as an independent unit to the area of Srebrenica in the course of the following day, 11 of July." Does that mean that they were in the area of Trnovo and from Trnovo they were being transferred to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in the area of Trnovo at that time, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since there seems to be a dilemma here over what exactly is the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and whether this unit was in Sarajevo and in Trnovo, I'd like to see document 1D288. We now see the document without translation. Can we see first the last page to see who sent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does it say Ljubisa Borovcanin here, at the bottom of the document, page 4?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, and I can confirm this is his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the electronic courtroom display again page 1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Before we move on to the questions, can you tell if you had occasion to see this document before and if you have studied?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm I have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I will now read out for the record the first page and tell you what it's about. This is a report by Mr. Borovcanin covering all the days of the Srebrenica operation, beginning with the 12th of July when he was sent there through the 20th July, which we can see on page 4. I will read the beginning: "Pursuant to an order by the deputy minister of the interior, number 64/95, dated 10 July, 1995, I have been assigned to participate together with part of the MUP forces in the Operation Srebrenica 95, which has been under way for five days now. "The said order specifies that the combat group of the MUP in this sector shall consist of the 2nd Special Police Detachment from Sekovici, the 1st Company of the PJP Zvornik, two companies of the joint forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and a company of the MUP from the centre for training on Jahorina. "The establishment of the combat group is scheduled for 11th July by 1200 hours. Out of the said forces, the 2nd Special Police Detachment of Sekovici was involved in combat operations in Srenje [phoen] at the moment when the order was issued. The 1st PJP Zvornik Company had not assembled," so it wasn't even assembled yet, "both companies of the MUP of the RSK were engaged in combat in Trnovo, while the company from the training centre was at its base on Jahorina." And Borovcanin adds: "I received this order at the forward command post in Trnovo where I was commanding the joint forces of the MUP." And my question is: Is there any reference to the MUP of Serbia in this order -- in this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see it right now. And I think there is no reference to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is there a reference to the MUP of Serbia on the 1st page? I am asking you this since you've told us that you studied the document. You speak Serbian, you read Serbian, you said it so yourself in the previous trials, you said that you use Serbian?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm there is no reference to MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown the second page, the third page, and finally the fourth page of the document. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is there a reference anywhere to the MUP of Serbia on the second page of Borovcanin's report? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see any.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now could the third page of the same report be shown to the witness in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is already on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, thank you, Mr. President. Can the witness be shown the fourth page then, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see any reference to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there are no references to the MUP of Serbia in the report of the commander who was in charge of those forces, what made you conclude that the MUP was Serbia participated in the action in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That MUP Serbia participated in action in Trnovo, we can see from two documents, at least we have been going over today. From 1st of July, you can see that they are in the area of Trnovo and the document from 10 of July where order of Tomo Kovac is withdrawing this unit from the area of Trnovo, so based on these two documents we can conclude that these unit was in that battle-field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you have studied this document, and in chronological terms it describes the events that took place on the 10th and then on the 11th, and then in the penultimate passage it describes the events on the 12th of July, 1995. And then the penultimate passage on the 3rd page describes the events on the 13th of July. And finally, the events on the 16th, the 15th, and the 14th July, and then on the 17th, 18th, 19th, and 20th of July on the 5th page of the document. My question is this: You speak the language, you studied the document, does Commander Borovcanin refer anywhere in the document to the presence of Skorpions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not, but in order to be 100 per cent sure, I would need to review this document more carefully just to find if there is any Skorpion reference, and I think that we have this document in English, so I am sure the OTP is having it in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we do have this document in English. It appears that it's not been uploaded in the e-court and we are in the process of uploading it into e-court, because as Mr. Gajic knows and General Tolimir knows, this is an important document, a central document in this case. It is 65 ter 5869. It involves Ljubisa Borovcanin, who you know was charged - and convicted, I should say - in the Popovic case in relation to his involvement in the events concerning Srebrenica. This document, as I understand it, is from September or thereabout of 1995. And it effectively recounts the involvement of Mr. Borovcanin and his unit in these events, so you can see that it post-dates the order that was actually issued that is now before the Trial Chamber. But we are endeavouring to get the English document uploaded in the e-court for your benefit, because I think it will resolve many of the issues that the accused has raised throughout this cross-examination. And I would add to the extent that it may be -- it may be of benefit to the Trial Chamber, I certainly can redirect Mr. Janc in this area and with this document in order to clarify these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye, for helping us to use the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And since there is an English version, and you said it yourself as a witness, was it used in any other trial before this Tribunal? Was this document considered or was the issue and the problem Skorpions ever considered in any of the other trials before this Tribunal? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am quite certain that it was an issue at the Popovic et al trial, but I cannot say anything about the other trials.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you study the entire documentation related to the issue of Skorpions in the case of the persons who were on trial before this Tribunal in the case known as Popovic et al?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure I studied a lot of documentation in relation to Skorpion -- Skorpions unit, but you never be sure if you reviewed and studied everything, because every day you can find something new. So -- and I would say most of the documentation I am sure aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I understand that this document that we have in front of us in e-court now apparently had had two 65 ter numbers. And the English version can be found under 65 ter number 87, and that might be appropriate to pull it up now so that we can all see what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope that can be found. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to thank Mr. Vanderpuye, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And now, can you tell us, please, did you study the documents presented by the Borovcanin Defence? And we know that Borovcanin was in charge of the Skorpion units in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am sure aware of most of documentation which was presented during the trial, so I can confirm that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us and the Trial Chamber whether any of the things that were committed by the Skorpions were something that those who were accused of the crimes in Srebrenica were charged with? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the Trnovo killings, this video, this killing of six Muslim men, this is the only one which -- which was committed by the Skorpions where the OTP indicted individuals in relation to that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. I asked you this: Since you studied the documentation that was provided by the Defence teams of the accused in the Srebrenica case, are there documents relative to Skorpions in the evidence of the individuals charged with the crimes in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know what -- what do you have in mind, so if you could be more precise I can say, yes, which documents you are referring to, but I think that I responded to you in general terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked whether there were any references made to the Skorpions in the Srebrenica trials. You studied the documents and you said that there were such documents. I am asking you whether any of the accused in those cases were charged with the murders comitted by Skorpions in Trnovo? Thank you. Maybe I am not precise enough. Has anybody been found guilty? Has anybody been convicted of those crimes? That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure. I would need to review the judgement again. So I think they were, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think you can see by the witness's somewhat tentative answer that it's really -- there is no relevance to the question to any material issue that's been presented through this witness, nor is it germane to the subject matter of the witness's testimony. Frankly, what the witness's knowledge is, as to who was convicted or not convicted of a given crime, is completely irrelevant to any material issue at this trial which, from our point of view, seeks to establish the General's guilt with respect to the crimes that are charged in the indictment which is not necessarily derivative of any other finding of guilt with respect to anybody else. So I don't really see what the point of relevance is to this line of questioning. If the General has a particular avenue in mind that he can articulate, that would be helpful. Otherwise, I just don't see any point in pursuing this particular line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question to the best of his knowledge today, and I think we are now in a situation that Mr. Tolimir has only one last question left, and then there are, perhaps, some procedural matters. Do you want to put another question or shall we leave it like this for today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. First of all let me explain the relevance of the matter. What is relevant here is the fact that the witness said that he read the documentation in respect of the Srebrenica cases that had to do with Trnovo. He studied all the materials relative to Trnovo. Second of all, I want this document to be admitted into evidence. We see the document both in English and in Serbian. This is a report that was looked at during the Srebrenica group trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness didn't say that he studied all materials relative to Trnovo, but probably most of it. This document will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document under 65 ter number 00087 will be assigned Exhibit D00130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For today this concludes the cross-examination of Mr. Janc. I am not sure when he will be called again into the courtroom for a continuation of the cross-examination. Perhaps Mr. Vanderpuye can give us an estimation, and especially for the benefit of Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think I have an answer. We should be able to put Mr. Janc back on the stand at the end of next week. We have arrangements for an interpreter, a Dutch interpreter to attend to the next witness. Follow that, we have an expert who has a small window of opportunity in which to give his testimony, and so we expect that we would be able to put Mr. Janc on at the end of next week. I think I have the following information for the Trial Chamber with respect to interpretations -- translations, I am sorry, with respect to the following exhibits: P00368 B, 65 ter number 3149 B, now has an English translation; the same for P00841 B, which is 65 ter 2904 B; the same for P00841 C, which is 65 ter 2904 E; and finally, P00854, which is 65 ter 6460. All of these have English translations now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. They are now exhibits. Is there anything else to raise before we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The only thing that comes to mind, Mr. President, is if Mr. Tolimir can tell us approximately how much he has left for Mr. Janc. That might be helpful also in terms of future scheduling. I might have a brief redirect for him as well, but that might be helpful to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Many new issues have been raised here. The witness has not studied all the documents. I expect him to make up for that and study them for when he next appears. The Defence will continue cross-examining him at any time chosen by the Court. We only want the truth to be known and we don't have a problem with him working for the OTP and being contacted by the OTP. In the meantime, all we care about is to clarify and get to the bottom of as many issues as possible, both during the cross-examination as well as during the re-examination by the OTP. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that you didn't give the Prosecution any indication about the length of your cross-examination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I said that bearing in mind the schedule of the witnesses who have been planned, we take into account all the reasons. We are not worried about the contacts that the witness may have with the OTP, and the OTP should be the ones to choose the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, there was only one question. Can you give a time estimation. That was all. We are under time pressure, we have to leave the courtroom. It will be needed for another Trial Chamber. Can you give a time estimation; yes or no? This is a very simple question. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that Mr. Vanderpuye and I will get in touch either today or tomorrow and we will deal with the issue of the time still necessary for the rest of the cross-examination, and I hope that the situation will be somewhat clearer on Monday or on Tuesday at the latest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be appreciated by the Chamber. We have to adjourn now. Mr. Janc, you have to come back at a later stage. Please bear in mind that you are not allowed to have contact about the content of your testimony during the break. We have to adjourn now and resume next Monday, the 1st of November, in the afternoon, quarter past 2.00 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
